transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-29
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sophie Delgado (Redwood AE), Marcus Huang (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Oxbow Head of ML), Liam Ortega (Oxbow Infra Lead), Dana Kim (Oxbow CTO)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on Oxbow's implementation plan: VPC connectivity, staging tenant, Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, initial success metrics for first 6 weeks, and security/compliance checklist. Agree to send network templates and pricing, run a short pilot in staging, and schedule a technical deep-dive next week.

Topics Covered:
- VPC peering / private deployment options
- Data residency and audit logging
- Dedicated capacity vs hosted burst model (cost/latency tradeoffs)
- Staging tenant and evaluation metrics (prompt sets, latency targets)
- Rollout cadence and support model

Quick action items recap (auto):
- Network diagram + checklist (Sophie)
- Dedicated pricing + SLOs (Marcus)
- Provide prompt examples and evaluation rubric (Priya)

Transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "Alright everyone, thanks for joining. We grabbed about 50 minutes, we wanted to run through the onboarding flow for Oxbow, make sure we have the VPC details, staging tenant, and any governance needs. Marcus is with me for the technical bits."
00:22 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "Hey all, good to meet you. I'll pick up the Dedicated capacity and the runtimes questions, also batching/quantization stuff later."
00:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): "Thanks. Quick context: we're building a customer-facing summarization + compliance assistant. Latency matters for front-end, cost matters for scale. We have strict audit needs, SOC2 in play, and data residency in our EU region for EU customers."
01:05 Speaker 4 (Liam): "From infra, we're AWS heavy (us-east-1 and eu-west-1), we use Transit Gateway and strict egress rules, so we'll need a VPC private connect or a dedicated peering option. Also curious about private deployment vs Redwood hosted api for PII handling."
01:40 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "Totally. We support hosted API for fast onboarding, Dedicated for reserved GPU pools, and Private (VPC) for air-gapped or regulated workloads. For egress/ingress we have a few patterns: VPC peering with NAT-proxied outbound, or customer-managed VPNs with static routes. We can provide a connectivity checklist."
02:05 Speaker 3 (Priya): "Is there an option to keep request logs out of the hosted plane? We need audit logs but redaction and minimal retention are key."
02:20 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "Yes, we can configure retention windows and push audit logs to your S3 or SIEM. For Private deployments you keep the control plane but data paths stay inside your VPC if that's the direction you want. There's a tradeoff in manageability vs latency depending on the choice."
03:00 Speaker 5 (Dana): "Curious about costs — if we start with hosted for a quick pilot then move to Dedicated for production, what's the typical migration path? How disruptive is model pinning/rollouts?"
03:30 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "Best practice is start with a hosted pilot to validate prompts and evals, then move to Dedicated with the same API surface. We support model pinning and can do canary rollouts. Migration usually means provisioning capacity and updating endpoint config, minimal code change on your side — mostly config and DNS/VPC steps."
04:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): "For our evals we track rouge/precision metrics and also hallucination counts on a labeled set. We want to measure latency under 250ms p95 for short prompts (<=256 tokens)."
04:40 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "250ms p95 for <=256 is feasible on Dedicated with appropriate batching disabled for low-latency paths; however batching can reduce cost significantly. We can show quantized model options that still meet that latency target."
05:15 Speaker 4 (Liam): "If we need KV cache persistence between requests for chat sessions, does Redwood's runtime support that in Private deployments? Heard some vendors call it K V cache but spelled funny in docs."
05:32 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "Yes, we support KV cache management and prefix caching. On Private deployments we can route the cache in-process to reduce round trips. There's a config flag for persistence vs ephemeral cache depending on throughput and memory footprint."
06:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): "Security questions: SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit trail, and HSM/KMS for key management — are those supported out of the box?"
06:28 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "SSO via SAML and RBAC roles are supported in the Console; for encryption we integrate with customer KMS or HSM for Private installs. We'll share the security pack and SOC2 documentation after the call."
07:00 Speaker 5 (Dana): "We also need to confirm data residency for EU traffic and whether embeddings or vector indexes are stored in region — that's a blocker for some customers."
07:18 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "Embeddings and KV caches can be configured to store in-region on Private or Dedicated, hosted by default is multi-region but we can pin model serving to eu-west-1 for EU traffic. We'll include the data residency patterns in the doc."
08:02 Speaker 3 (Priya): "Timeline: we want a pilot with 2-3 endpoints and 1k daily active users by mid-December. Is that realistic?"
08:20 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "Yes, that's a reasonable runway. Next 2 weeks we should get networking, then provision staging tenant, run functional tests, then production cutover in a 4-6 week window depending on networking and security review."
09:00 Speaker 4 (Liam): "Operationally we'll need runbooks and a rollback plan — e.g., if a new model causes regressions, can we fallback quickly to prior versions?"
09:22 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "We have rollout policies with automatic fallback to pinned variants on error thresholds. Rollbacks are a config change and we can automate with A/B testing rules in Console."
10:05 Speaker 3 (Priya): "One more: prompt auditing. We need to keep a copy of prompts used for compliance for 90 days and make them queryable by case id."
10:20 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "We can route prompts to your S3 with masking options. We'll add the retention config to the checklist."
11:05 Speaker 6 (Unknown / muffled): "(inaudible) — can you repeat the dedicated cost model?"
11:12 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "Sure: Dedicated is a monthly reserved capacity model with GPU pools. Pricing depends on GPU class and committed throughput. There's an overage / burst pricing tier for occasional spikes. We'll send a sample pricing matrix."
12:00 Speaker 5 (Dana): "Are there compliance attestations for on-prem or private installs? We have auditors who ask for deployment diagrams."
12:28 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "Yes, Private deployments have a deployment package with architecture diagrams and we provide SOC2 artifacts where applicable. We'll share the compliance pack and a template diagram for your auditors."
13:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): "For the pilot, do you recommend we start with a smaller model quantized to 4-bit to save cost? Will that affect hallucination rates?"
13:32 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "Quantization can drop cost a lot with small quality impact for many tasks. We'll run a quick eval; for safety-critical summarization we typically test 4-bit and 8-bit variants and compare. We'll set up an eval harness for you."
14:05 Speaker 4 (Liam): "Network details: we use strict egress and only allow specific IP ranges; can Redwood support static egress IPs for peering?"
14:20 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "Yes, we can provide static egress IPs for peering or use customer-managed NAT gateways. We'll include the IP ranges in the network checklist."
15:00 Speaker 3 (Priya): "Who will be our primary contacts for triage during the pilot? We need an escalation path for incidents impacting latency or hallucinations affecting compliance."
15:18 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "I'll be primary CSM/AE for coordination, Marcus will be SE for tech triage, and we can add an ops SLA engineer if you go Dedicated. We'll capture escalation paths in the runbook."
16:10 Speaker 5 (Dana): "Ok, let's talk about metrics: we want p95 latency, token cost per request, and hallucination rate as measured on labeled set. Also alert thresholds to kick off rollback."
16:35 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "Console exposes token-level cost and latency, and you can hook up quality monitoring to trigger regression alerts if the eval set shows >X% drop in accuracy. We'll show examples."
17:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): "Regarding embeddings storage — can we control retention and encryption at rest per embedding store?"
17:28 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "Yes, retention and encryption are configurable and we can offer in-region vector stores for Dedicated/Private. We'll note that in the security doc."
18:02 Speaker 4 (Liam): "Operational concern: will you require us to open inbound ports? Our security team frowns on that."
18:20 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "Inbound is generally not required for hosted — we call out to your environment. For Private we may require a small set of management ports for the control plane; we'll document minimal port requirements."
19:00 Speaker 3 (Priya): "Anything else for rollout? I want to ensure we have a stoplight plan for go/no-go decisions."
19:12 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "We recommend a 3-stage plan: staging smoke tests, limited-canary with 5% traffic, then full ramp. Each stage has quality gates tied to your evals and latency SLOs."
20:00 Speaker 5 (Dana): "Let's lock next steps: Sophie, you'll send the network checklist and SOC2 pack; Marcus will send pricing and propose SE deep-dive slots next week; we'll confirm CIDRs and internal timelines."
20:18 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "Yes. I'll send everything by Monday EOD. Marcus, can you propose two slots for the deep-dive?"
20:26 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "Sure — Wednesday and Friday morning PT work for me, I'll send a calendar invite."
20:40 Speaker 3 (Priya): "When can we get a staging tenant? We want to run initial prompts within 48 hours of network setup."
20:52 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "We can provision a staging tenant as soon as we have the network allowlist and a staging admin — typical lead time 1-3 business days."
21:10 Speaker 4 (Liam): "I'll get the CIDR ranges and firewall policy to Sophie by Monday morning. Also we'll include the contact for networking."
21:30 Speaker 5 (Dana): "One last question: logging — can we redact PII automatically before logs are stored?"
21:42 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "We have masking hooks and pre-processing pipelines. For sensitive PII we can do client-side redaction or on-ingress filters. We'll include recommended patterns in the checklist."
22:10 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "Great. Recap of next steps: docs, pricing, staging, and deep-dive. Any final items?"
22:22 Speaker 3 (Priya): "Nope, sounds good. Thanks everyone."
22:28 Speaker 5 (Dana): "Thanks, appreciate the clarity."
22:35 Speaker 2 (Marcus): "Thanks all, will follow up with the technical artifacts."
22:40 Speaker 1 (Sophie): "Meeting end."

Note on transcription: occasional overlap and brief audio dropout around 11:05-11:12; some proper nouns (e.g., "KV cache") may be spelled out or mis-transcribed in the automated transcript.

End of transcript.
